items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Lester and I would still be sitting in there until sun-up, sometimes 10 o'clock in the morning, just he and playing.

ctx.x: understand happened when I just happened not to be on the scene -- Lester Young's thing with Paul Jones. I got stories about it... Always stories like that are conflicting, you know. Naturally, Phil and Otto, being from out West and everything, and having a different feeling about things... Phil could give you the impression that Lester had walked in and walked all over top of Paul, you know. Well, I wasn't there, so I can't say. But I know that Paul was an excellent saxophone player, and there's no question…

But I got to know Lester, and from then on, after that, when Lester came in town, soon as he got off the bus he was right in this club. There were times when, after this fellow, Toby Walker, had finished playing up there and everybody would go home -- that's usually around 5 o'clock in the morning -- Lester and I would still be sitting in there until sun-up, sometimes 10 o'clock in the morning, just he and playing. Which I was happy to do, because at that particular time he was recording with Billie Holiday and…
